back: P = problems solvable in polynomial time. NP = problems whose solutions can be verified in polynomial time.

front: What does it mean for a problem to be NP-complete?
back: It is in NP (verifiable in poly time) AND NP-hard (every problem in NP reduces to it in poly time) — the hardest problems in NP.

front: If a single NP-complete problem were solved in polynomial time, what would follow?
back: P = NP, and every problem in NP would also be solvable in polynomial time.

front: What is the seed NP-complete problem most reductions chain back to?
back: SAT (Boolean satisfiability), proven NP-complete directly via the Cook-Levin theorem.

front: Practically, what should you reach for when a problem is shown NP-complete?
back: Approximation algorithms, heuristics/metaheuristics, or exact exponential-time algorithms with pruning (backtracking) for small inputs.
